title: Discrete and continuous variables; nominal, ordinal, interval and ratio scales

videos.script: Lesson one split the columns into two families. Names on one side, quantities on the other. This lesson splits each family again, because the split decides what arithmetic you are allowed to do. {{families}} Start with the quantities. Some are counts. Three items, seven items, never seven and a half. Others are measurements, and a delivery can take thirty-four point five minutes or anything in between. {{discrete}} Now the names. Pix and card have no order at all. But a rating of one to five stars does have an order. Five is better than four. {{ordinal}} Is the step from four to five the same size as the step from one to two? Nobody measured that. So an average of star ratings is a number resting on an assumption. {{steps}} Then the quantities with a zero that means nothing. Twenty-seven degrees is not twice as warm as thirteen and a half. Change to Fahrenheit and twice becomes one point four three. {{temperature}} Four scales come out of this. Nominal, ordinal, interval and ratio. Each one allows everything the one below it allows, and one thing more. {{ladder}} By the end you will look at a column, name its scale, and know which summary it can carry. {{summary}}
